explanation: When the model looked at the abstract, it found the key words "massive ascites" and "abnormal peritoneal tissue" (which we can think of as "absence" of the normal, healthy peritoneums). "Ascites" is a build-up of fluid in the abdomen, which can be very serious. "Peritoneum," on the other hand, is the lining of the abdomen. When it's "absent" or "destroyed," it can't do its job, which is to help keep the organs in place. The model likely thought, "This patient's body can't keep its organs in the right place, and there's too much fluid around them. " That's why it classified this as a "digestive system disease."
